title: Vitamin-M (with poem: I Cannot Remember My Mother)

topics.title: Family and mothers: words of love and care

learn.hook: Who remembers to pack your tiffin, even on the busiest morning? Families speak love in a hundred quiet ways.
points: The lesson 'Vitamin-M' is a family story about a boy, Ravi, and his grandfather, whose memory has grown weak. It shows that elders need patience, care and respect from their family, and its paired poem by Tagore remembers a mother.
Words of care: nurture (care for and help to grow), affection (fondness, gentle love), devotion (deep loyalty and love), cherish (hold dear), sacrifice (give up something for someone else).

Family phrasal verbs: bring up (raise a child), look after (take care of), take after (resemble an older family member), get along with (have a friendly relationship), look up to (admire and respect).
Idioms: 'the apple of someone's eye' means a person who is very dear; 'runs in the family' means a quality shared by many family members.
Writers often show love through actions rather than words. Readers infer feelings from what characters do.

example.q: Read: 'Amma's alarm rings at five. By the time Ishaan wakes up, his tiffin is packed, his uniform ironed and a glass of warm haldi milk waits on the table. Amma only says, "Drink it before it gets cold." Ishaan smiles; he knows that is her way of saying "I love you."' How does Amma show her love?
steps: Look at what Amma does: wakes early, packs the tiffin, irons the uniform, warms milk.
Look at what she says: only a simple reminder.
Ishaan's thought tells us her actions carry the message of love.
example.answer: She shows her love through caring actions rather than many words.

learn.reallife: Next time someone in your family keeps the last piece of mithai for you, you'll know it is love in action!

items.text: Riya is the ___ of her grandfather's eye.
Musical talent runs in the ___; her mother and aunt both sing.
Aarav really takes ___ his father; they have the same smile.
My aunt brought ___ three children while working full-time.

quiz.q: What does 'nurture' mean?
options: To care for and help to grow
quiz.explain: To nurture is to look after someone or something and help it develop.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word and guesses a negative meaning

quiz.q: What does 'look after' mean in 'Didi looks after our baby brother'?
quiz.explain: 'Look after' means to take care of someone.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'look after' with 'look for' or 'take after'

quiz.q: 'Meera looks up to her mother.' What does this mean?
options: Meera is taller than her mother
Meera admires and respects her mother
quiz.explain: To look up to someone is to admire and respect them.
quiz.mistake: Takes 'look up' in its literal sense of raising the eyes

quiz.q: Read: 'Papa never says much, but every night he quietly covers Tara with a blanket after she falls asleep.' What can you infer about Papa?
options: He wants Tara to wake up
quiz.explain: His quiet nightly action shows care, even without words.
quiz.mistake: Expects love to be shown only in words

quiz.q: Which word is a synonym of 'affection'?
quiz.explain: Affection is a gentle feeling of love, which is fondness.
quiz.mistake: Picks a strong feeling that is not love

quiz.q: What does 'the apple of someone's eye' mean?
options: A person who is very dear to someone
Someone who eats a lot of apples
quiz.explain: The idiom describes a person someone loves and treasures greatly.
quiz.mistake: Reads the idiom literally

quiz.q: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
quiz.explain: For one mother, the possessive is mother + 's: mother's.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the apostrophe or puts it in the wrong place

quiz.q: What is the antonym of 'cherish'?
quiz.explain: To cherish is to hold dear; to neglect is to fail to care for.
quiz.mistake: Picks a synonym instead of an antonym

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: "My mother bird never says 'I love you'. Does she love me?"
teach.praise: Chirp! Love is shown through caring actions, like bringing worms every morning. My mother bird loves me!
teach.nudge: Hmm, if she doesn't say it, how else could she show it?

topics.title: Talking in the family: reported speech

learn.hook: Your little brother runs to you: 'Ma said you have to come home now!' He has just used reported speech!
points: Direct speech gives the exact words in quotation marks: Ma said, "I am tired." Reported (indirect) speech gives the meaning without quotation marks: Ma said that she was tired.
When the reporting verb is in the past, tenses usually move one step back: am/is → was, are → were, will → would, can → could, present perfect → past perfect.
Pronouns and time or place words change: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, now → then, here → there. 'Said to' becomes 'told'.
Questions: yes/no questions use 'asked if/whether'; wh-questions keep the wh-word but use normal word order (asked where I was going).
Commands and requests use told/asked/requested + object + to + verb; a negative command uses 'not to'.

example.q: Change into reported speech: Ma said to me, "I am making kheer today."
steps: 'I' (Ma) becomes 'she'; 'am making' moves back to 'was making'.
example.answer: Ma told me that she was making kheer that day.

learn.reallife: When you pass on a message from your teacher to your parents, you are using reported speech: 'Ma'am said that the PTM is on Saturday.'

games.title: Build the reported sentence
games.prompt: Arrange to report: Nani said to me, "Sit near me."
items: Nani
told me
to sit
near
her.

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Ma said, "I am tired."
options: Ma said that I am tired.
Ma said that she was tired.
Ma said that she is tiring.
Ma told that she was tired.
quiz.explain: 'I' becomes 'she' and 'am' moves back to 'was'. 'Said' with no listener stays 'said'.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change the pronoun or the tense, or uses 'told' without an object

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Papa said to me, "Close the door."
options: Papa told me to close the door.
Papa told me that close the door.
Papa said me to close the door.
Papa told me closing the door.
quiz.explain: A command becomes told + object + to + verb.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'that' with a command or 'said me' instead of 'told me'

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Dadi said to me, "Have you eaten lunch?"
options: Dadi asked me have I eaten lunch.
Dadi asked me that had I eaten lunch.
Dadi asked me if I had eaten lunch.
Dadi told me if I ate lunch.
quiz.explain: A yes/no question uses 'asked if', normal word order, and the present perfect moves back to the past perfect.
quiz.mistake: Keeps question word order or uses 'that' in a reported question

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Didi said to me, "Where are you going?"
options: Didi asked me where was I going.
Didi asked me where I was going.
Didi asked me where are you going.
Didi told me where I go.
quiz.explain: Keep 'where', use normal order (I was going) and move the tense back.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the question word order in reported speech

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Mother said to Riya, "Don't touch the hot pan."
options: Mother told Riya to not touching the hot pan.
Mother told Riya don't touch the hot pan.
Mother told Riya that not touch the hot pan.
Mother told Riya not to touch the hot pan.
quiz.explain: A negative command becomes told + object + not to + verb.
quiz.mistake: Keeps 'don't' or places 'not' wrongly

quiz.q: In reported speech, what does 'tomorrow' usually become?
quiz.explain: When reporting later, 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' or 'the following day'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the next day with the previous day

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Ravi said, "I will help Ma."
options: Ravi said that he would help Ma.
Ravi said that I will help Ma.
Ravi said that he will helped Ma.
Ravi said he helps Ma yesterday.
quiz.explain: 'I' becomes 'he' and 'will' moves back to 'would'.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change 'will' to 'would'

quiz.q: Choose the reported form: Nana said to me, "Please pass the salt."
options: Nana requested me that pass the salt.
Nana requested me passing the salt.
Nana requested to me to pass the salt.
Nana requested me to pass the salt.
quiz.explain: A polite request uses requested/asked + object + to + verb.
quiz.mistake: Adds 'that' or 'to me' to a reported request

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: "Ma said, 'I am hungry.' How do I tell Papa what she said without the quote marks?"
teach.praise: Tweet! 'Ma said that she was hungry.' Change the pronoun, step back the tense, add 'that'. Got it!
teach.nudge: Almost! What happens to 'I' and to 'am' when you report it?

topics.title: Tagore's poem on memory: senses and feelings

learn.hook: Can a smell bring back a person? Catch a whiff of jasmine and suddenly you are in Nani's courtyard again!
points: Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941) was a poet, writer, composer and painter from Bengal. In 1913 he won the Nobel Prize in Literature and became the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize.
Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', India's national anthem, and founded Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan.
In his poem 'I Cannot Remember My Mother', the speaker cannot clearly recall his mother, yet feels her presence in everyday sounds, scents and sights.
Memory poems often use sensory imagery and a nostalgic tone. Nostalgia is a warm, slightly sad longing for the past.
'Used to' + verb describes a past habit that no longer happens: 'Nani used to sing while she cooked.'

example.q:
Read this original poem:
'I cannot see Nani's face so clear,
Yet when the evening kettle sings
Or jasmine scent drifts softly near,
I feel her close in little things.
Her lullabies still hum in rain;
She's far, yet always comes again.'
Which senses bring back the memory, and what is the tone?
steps: 'the evening kettle sings' and 'lullabies' are sounds: hearing.
The speaker misses Nani but feels comforted, so the tone is tender and nostalgic.
example.answer: Hearing and smell bring back the memory; the tone is tender and nostalgic.

learn.reallife: The smell of a particular agarbatti, the tune of an old film song or the taste of a festival sweet can bring back a loved one in a flash.

games.title: Which sense does the image touch?
items: The orange glow of a diya
A golden autumn sky
Peacock feathers shining blue and green
A kettle whistling
Temple bells ringing
Mustard seeds crackling in hot oil
Jasmine at dusk
The aroma of ghee on hot rotis
The scent of wet earth after rain

games.title: Tagore and the poem
items: Tagore was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize.
He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
Tagore wrote 'Vande Mataram'.
'Vande Mataram' was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana'.
Tagore was also a composer and a painter.
He composed thousands of songs and also painted.
Nostalgia is a feeling of fear about the future.
Nostalgia is a longing for the past.
'Used to' can describe a habit in the past.
'She used to sing' means she sang regularly in the past.
In the original poem, the jasmine scent is an image of smell.
A scent is something we smell.

quiz.q: For which field did Rabindranath Tagore win the Nobel Prize in 1913?
quiz.explain: Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a famous Nobel field without knowing Tagore was a writer

quiz.q: Which national song or anthem did Tagore write?
quiz.explain: Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', which is India's national anthem.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the national anthem with other famous patriotic songs

quiz.q: Where did Tagore found Visva-Bharati?
quiz.explain: Visva-Bharati was founded by Tagore at Santiniketan in West Bengal.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where Tagore's school and university are

quiz.q: 'Yet when the evening kettle sings.' The kettle 'singing' is an example of:
quiz.explain: A kettle cannot really sing; giving it a human action is personification.
quiz.mistake: Calls any striking image a simile

quiz.q: 'Or jasmine scent drifts softly near.' Which sense does this line appeal to?
quiz.explain: 'Scent' is something we smell.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all imagery is about sight

quiz.q: What does 'nostalgic' mean?
options: Full of tender longing for the past
quiz.explain: Being nostalgic means feeling a warm, slightly sad longing for past times.
quiz.mistake: Links the word with the future instead of the past

quiz.q: What does 'used to' show in 'Nani used to tell us stories every night'?
options: A habit in the past that no longer happens
quiz.explain: 'Used to' + verb shows a regular past habit.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'used to' means 'being accustomed to' something now

quiz.q: 'She's far, yet always comes again.' What tone do these lines suggest?
quiz.explain: The speaker misses Nani but finds comfort that she 'comes again' in memory.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the hopeful word 'yet'

teach.ask: Gappu sniffs a jasmine flower: "Why does this smell remind me of my grandmother bird? How do poets use that?"
teach.praise: Chirp! Poets use smells and sounds to bring back memories, and the feeling is nostalgic. Hello, Grandma bird!
teach.nudge: But how exactly does a smell or a sound help the poet remember someone?
